current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens the unit, כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חֲרָדָ֖ה שָׁמָ֑עְנוּ פַּ֖חַד וְאֵ֥ין שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte), matching “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5) “We have heard a voice of trembling; a voice of fear, and not of peace.” (web:Jer.30.5) — a communal cry of dread rather than a report about a third party. The day named next carries the hoy interjection in its own DAY-ALAS shape, not a woe-oracle onset: ה֗וֹי כִּ֥י גָד֛וֹל הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מֵאַ֣יִן כָּמֹ֑הוּ וְעֵֽת צָרָ֥ה הִיא֙ לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּמִמֶּ֖נָּה יִוָּשֵֽׁעַ (oshb:Jer.30.7, byte), matching “Alas, for that day is great, so that none is like it! It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he will be saved out of it.” (web:Jer.30.7) — an exclamation over the day's own severity rather than a pronounced judgment against a named party, closing already on the promise of rescue rather than on threat alone. Jacob's name in this same verse carries the defective spelling these bytes attest. A day-formula turn follows at verse 8, וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק וְלֹא יַעַבְדוּ ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte), matching “It will come to pass in that day, says Yahweh of Armies, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds. Strangers will no more make them their bondservants;” (web:Jer.30.8) — the second-person singular marking here is real but mixed with a third-person suffix in the same clause and a third-person reference closing the same verse; a full neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack sits inside this same verse, corroborating rather than opening a fresh unit, since no koh-amar or date-formula onset of its own accompanies it. The rescue promise continues through the same defective spelling of Jacob's name twice over, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte), matching “Therefore don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says Yahweh. Don’t be dismayed, Israel. For, behold, I will save you from afar, and save your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.” (web:Jer.30.10). It closes on כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte), matching “For I am with you, says Yahweh, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.” (web:Jer.30.11). A second fresh koh-amar turns the address to a feminine-singular figure at verse 12, and this row stops there.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 8's own bayom-hahu turn to the broken yoke was considered: that verse carries the span's first second-person singular marking, אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte); it is rejected because no koh-amar or date-formula onset stands at that verse, the marking is mixed with a third-person suffix in the same clause and a third-person reference closing the same verse, the person layer reverts to third person at the very next verse, וְעָ֣בְד֔וּ אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֵת֙ דָּוִ֣ד (oshb:Jer.30.9, byte), and the first vocative addressee in the unit stands only two verses later, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte); the day-formula opening the verse is a day-alas-adjacent shape distinct from the year-header date object and stands in 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys), so it is not read here as a date-formula onset. The day-formula turn is left as one of this stretch's unresolved internal questions rather than folded into either reading.

A second-person plural imperative pair opens the interior comparison, שַׁאֲלוּ נָ֣א (oshb:Jer.30.6, byte), standing inside the span without a fresh koh-amar of its own.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The address turns to a feminine-singular figure under a fresh koh-amar, כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֵֽךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte), matching “For Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.30.12) “Your hurt is incurable. Your wound is grievous.” (web:Jer.30.12) — an accusation-shaped wound complaint distinct in addressee from the collective ‘Jacob’/‘Israel’ material just closed. The complaint continues, naming the cause directly, מַה תִּזְעַק֙ עַל שִׁבְרֵ֔ךְ אָנ֖וּשׁ מַכְאֹבֵ֑ךְ עַ֣ל רֹ֣ב עֲוֺנֵ֗ךְ עָֽצְמוּ֙ חַטֹּאתַ֔יִךְ עָשִׂ֥יתִי אֵ֖לֶּה לָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.30.15, byte), matching “Why do you cry over your injury? Your pain is incurable. For the greatness of your iniquity, because your sins have increased, I have done these things to you.” (web:Jer.30.15); a paseq falls in this same verse. It closes on the reversal itself and the figure's own name, כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִדָּחָה֙ קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֔ךְ צִיּ֣וֹן הִ֔יא דֹּרֵ֖שׁ אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.30.17, byte), matching “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” (web:Jer.30.17) “because they have called you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’” (web:Jer.30.17) — Zion, named outright as the one this wound-and-healing address concerns. A third fresh koh-amar turns the address to Jacob's tents at verse 18, and this row does not reach past that turn.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 12 through 16 alone as a judgment_oracle was considered, since the wound and iniquity language there is accusatory in shape and no messenger or closure formula stands anywhere across Jer.30.13-Jer.30.16 to divide it from what follows (sweep: 1 verse each, span-scoped); it is rejected because the unit's own close at verse 17 resolves unambiguously into healing and restoration, and because the verse-initial לָכֵ֞ן inside that very grouping, standing so in exactly 2 verses across MT chs 29-31 (oshb:Jer.30.16, byte; sweep: 2 verses, verse-initial), turns the announcement toward the wound's own agents one verse before the alternative's own close, telling against rather than for treating it as separable.
current_row.literature_type_guess: incurable-wound complaint reversed into a healing promise

current_row.boundary_rationale: The address turns again under a fresh koh-amar, now to Jacob's tents rather than the feminine-singular figure just addressed, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִי שָׁב֙ שְׁבוּת֙ אָהֳלֵ֣י יַֽעֲק֔וֹב וּמִשְׁכְּנֹתָ֖יו אֲרַחֵ֑ם וְנִבְנְתָ֥ה עִיר֙ עַל תִּלָּ֔הּ וְאַרְמ֖וֹן עַל מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ יֵשֵֽׁב (oshb:Jer.30.18, byte), matching “Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.18) “Behold, I will reverse the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. The city will be built on its own hill, and the palace will be inhabited in its own place.” (web:Jer.30.18) — Jacob's name in this same verse carries the PLENE spelling these bytes attest (an added vav before the final letter), contrasted with the defective spelling attested twice over at verse 10 and once at verse 7 within this same range. The material through verse 21 stays third person, אַדִּיר֜וֹ מִמֶּ֗נּוּ וּמֹֽשְׁלוֹ֙ מִקִּרְבּ֣וֹ יֵצֵ֔א (oshb:Jer.30.21, byte), and the covenant formula that follows turns to second-person plural without a fresh speech formula of its own, וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte), matching “You shall be my people, and I will be your God.” (web:Jer.30.22) — no koh-amar or messenger formula accompanies the turn, so it does not reach the internal-seam classes that cut; a setumah falls in this same verse. A wrath-storm coda follows, addressed to the same audience though naming the divine subject in the third person now, לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה עַד עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ בָֽהּ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), matching “The fierce anger of Yahweh will not return until he has accomplished, and until he has performed the intentions of his heart. In the latter days you will understand it.” (web:Jer.30.24); a paseq also falls at oshb:Jer.30.23. The unit closes on a hinge verse that restates the covenant formula in universalized form, בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽהְיֶה֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים לְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ לִ֥י לְעָֽם (oshb:Jer.31.1, byte), matching “At that time,” says Yahweh, (web:Jer.31.1) “I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they will be my people.” (web:Jer.31.1) — naming all the families of Israel rather than Judah alone. A fresh koh-amar opens a wilderness-scene oracle at verse 2, and this row is held to end just before it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening verse 1 as the first verse of the following wilderness-grace oracle (verses 2 through 6) rather than as the close of this one was seriously weighed, since its own temporal opening phrase and its universalized covenant formula both look forward as much as back. It is held here instead because no koh-amar, addressee shift, or discourse imperative opens verse 1 itself — the next such onset is the koh-amar that actually begins verse 2 — so under the rule that rows cut only at fresh tier-1 onsets, verse 1 stays with the material it caps rather than the material it precedes; this attachment is held at reduced confidence as one of this range's own genuinely open seam questions.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Jacob's-tents restoration oracle with a wrath coda

current_row.device_notes: A setumah sits at this span's own front seam, oshb:Jer.30.17. A further setumah recurs inside the span at oshb:Jer.30.22. A third setumah closes the span itself at oshb:Jer.31.1 (WLC, single-witness throughout; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum). A paseq falls at oshb:Jer.30.18 and again at oshb:Jer.30.23 (WLC, single-witness, seg layer, count-only). Jacob's PLENE spelling at verse 18 is swept here per its own attested form, distinct from the defective spelling carried at verses 7 and 10 of this same range. The wrath-storm coda recurs at byte tier against Jer.23.19-Jer.23.20: הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה and עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte for each) together with עַד עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte) each stand in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses each, skeleton tier), disclosed here as texture rather than a boundary driver; the divergence stands in סַ֖עַר מִתְגּוֹרֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) against וְסַ֖עַר מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.23.19, byte), an added חֲרוֹן֙ and its own pointing of בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte for each), and one extra closing word at the Jer.23.20 counterpart, בִּינָֽה (oshb:Jer.23.20, byte). The divine name is named in the third person twice in this same coda, הִנֵּ֣ה סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.23, byte) and לֹ֣א יָשׁ֗וּב חֲרוֹן֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.24, byte), immediately after the first-person covenant clause וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte); the audience stays second-person plural across that turn. The covenant formula flips person again at the span's own close: third-person plural וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ לִ֥י לְעָֽם (oshb:Jer.31.1, byte) against the second-person plural וִהְיִ֥יתֶם לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם at verse 22 (oshb:Jer.30.22, byte).

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar opens a wilderness scene, third person throughout with no addressee of its own, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מָצָ֥א חֵן֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר עַ֖ם שְׂרִ֣ידֵי חָ֑רֶב הָל֥וֹךְ לְהַרְגִּיע֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte), matching “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.31.2) “The people who survive the sword found favor in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.” (web:Jer.31.2) — a memory of the exodus wandering rather than the tent-and-city imagery just closed.
